title: RBAC v2: Golden permissions coverage matrix and fuzz regression suite
creator: Priya Patel
description: Expand and harden the RBAC v2 permission testing framework by introducing a Golden Coverage Matrix and a permission-fuzz regression suite. This ticket covers: 1) authoring a canonical set of golden fixtures for role/permission combinations across Console, API, and Dedicated/Private surfaces; 2) implementing a deterministic fuzz runner that generates unlikely but valid permission states (edge combinations) and replays them against the gates; 3) CI integration so the regression suite runs on PRs touching RBAC/authorization codepaths and nightly builds; 4) linking audit log assertions so we can validate that permission denials/accepts are properly recorded for compliance; 5) capturing SSO/SAML-edge cases (group-to-role mappings, missing attributes) in fixtures; and 6) an operational playbook for regenerating goldens when behavior changes are intentional.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical Golden Coverage Matrix exists as versioned fixtures that cover >90% of prioritized role-permission permutations (per security PM matrix)
A permission-fuzz runner can generate and execute 10k unique permission states in under 2 hours on CI hardware and produces deterministic diffs against goldens
CI gates fail PRs with non-intentional golden diffs and provide a human-readable diagnostic to triage the regression
Audit log assertions are embedded in at least three fixture scenarios (console UI action, API token action, and service-to-service call) and validated in CI
SSO/SAML attribute-mapping edge cases are represented in fixtures and have one end-to-end test covering group->role and missing-attribute fallback paths
Playbook documented in Confluence with steps to regenerate, review, and approve golden changes (includes required security_review tag)
steps: Design Golden Coverage Matrix with Security PM and Design to select prioritized permutations
Extend existing test harness to accept matrix-driven fixtures and to correlate responses with audit logs
Implement permission-fuzz generator with seed-based determinism and tagging for slow/expensive cases
Wire regression suite into GitHub Actions workflow; enforce a nightly job and PR job with sampling
Add SSO/SAML fixture templates and a mocked IdP harness for end-to-end validation in CI
Create Confluence playbook and a cherrypick process for golden updates; route through security review
notes: We should keep golden fixtures small and composable to minimize churn — use param templates and include only deltas for large matrices
Consider using our k-v cache snapshots to speed up fuzz runs that reproduce long-lived session behavior
Talk with infra about a temporary larger CI runner for the full nightly 10k permutations — cost estimation required
Related effort: ENG-7890 covers audit-log schema stabilization which this suite will assert against; coordinate before merging
